findings.title: canManage() lets an admin with only the `view` scope manage groups.
findings.body: `canManage()` returns true when the all-groups permission grants either `VIEW` or `MANAGE`. An admin who was given only view access to all groups therefore passes `requireManage()`, which guards operations such as creating top-level groups. That is a privilege escalation from view to manage. Only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` should be accepted here, matching `canManage(GroupModel)`.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource IDs where group IDs are expected.
findings.body: Group resources are created with the group ID as their *name* (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()`, and the resource is created by name with a generated ID). This loop passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission`, which looks the resource up with `findByName`. That lookup misses and falls back to the all-groups resource, so the check runs against the wrong resource. The loop also adds the resource ID, not the group ID, to the result. That set goes into `UserModel.GROUPS` and the user-count queries, so admins with per-group `view-members` or `manage-members` either see no users or are evaluated against the wrong permission. It also includes the 'Groups' type resource itself. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the check and the returned value, and skip the type resource. I could not check how `ResourceStore.create` assigns IDs; if the ID always equals the name, this does not apply.
